params.body:
## Why

`MAIL_ALWAYS_TO` is what makes a real sender testable outside production: every outgoing
message is redirected there and the original recipients, cc and bcc included, disappear, so
none of the 542 dealers in the staging copy of the production database receives anything.

Until now the key held exactly one address. A test mail on staging therefore had one reader,
while the people who need to see it are two: the operator and the client's key user. The
alternative was forwarding by hand, which is not the same mail.

## What changed

- `MailRedirect::addresses(): list<string>` splits the key on commas (semicolons and stray
  whitespace are tolerated), trims every part, validates each with `FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL` and
  drops duplicates. `address()` stays as the singular helper (the first address) for callers
  that only need one; `active()` is true as soon as one valid address remains.
- `apply()` hands the whole list to `Mail::alwaysTo()`, so every address on it gets the same copy.
- `stocklist:smoke mail` names every redirect address, in both the configuration line and the
  "the redirect wins" warning after a `--mail-to` send. You are supposed to know who reads
  along before you press enter.
- `.env.example`, `config/mail.php`, `CUTOVER.md` and the CLAUDE.md gotcha say the key takes
  one or more addresses separated by commas.

## How an invalid entry behaves

It is skipped, and the rest of the list still receives. A typo in one address must not take the
other recipient down with it, and a broken send would be the worse failure of the two.

A list with nothing valid left over counts as not configured: `addresses()` returns empty,
`active()` is false, and `Outbound::mailOpen()` therefore keeps the mailer on `log`. That gate
is unchanged and still needs both locks - `mail` in `OUTBOUND_IMPACT` **and** at least one valid
catch-all address. Whitespace or garbage never opens the mailer, which is what keeps a dealer
from ever receiving something from a non-production environment.

## Production note

On production this key must stay EMPTY (and `APP_DEBUG=false`). A value here silently swallows
all dealer mail: the message leaves, it just never arrives. Nothing in this change alters that;
`Outbound::seal()` does not run on production at all.

## Checked

`php artisan test --filter='MailRedirect|Mail|Outbound|IntegrationSmoke|Smoke'` - 163 tests, 315
assertions, green, against MySQL loaded from `database/schema/mysql-schema.sql` plus the
post-2026-07-28 migrations, the way CI does it.

New tests in `MailRedirectTest` (it uses the array transport rather than `Mail::fake()`, because
a fake ignores `alwaysTo`): two addresses both receive and the original to, cc and bcc are gone;
a semicolon separates too; one valid plus one garbage entry sends to the valid one only;
only-garbage counts as not configured and the seal stays on `log`; a single address behaves
exactly as before. Plus one in `IntegrationSmokeTest`: the smoke line names every address.
params.title: Mail: redirect to more than one address
